vi: người giám sát, quản lý trực tiếp
en: A person who manages and checks the work of others.
example: I'm Kaeden, one of the supervisors.

en: To deal with or arrange something.
example: There are a few practical things you need to sort out this morning.

en: A small card or pin that shows who you are.
example: Show my letter of appointment and pick up my badge.

en: A small cupboard with a lock for personal things.
example: Put your coat and rucksack in one of the lockers there.

vi: hạn bán (hạn cuối để bán sản phẩm)
en: The last date on which a shop should sell a food item.
example: The first job is to check sell-by dates on the bread and cakes.

en: A room where goods are kept.
example: So you should bring more from the storeroom.

en: Designed to keep heat in.
example: Make sure you put on thermal gloves when you take anything out of the cold-room.

en: Damage to the body caused by extreme cold.
example: The temperature's low enough in there to get frostbite from touching things.

en: A lung condition that makes breathing difficult.
example: Especially if you suffer from something like heart condition or asthma.

en: Doing something regularly in the same way.
example: But you need to be consistent, so aim to train regularly.

vi: làm nản lòng, khiến mất hứng
en: To make someone not want to do something.
example: New members often say to me that they've been put off running.

en: Needing a lot of time, effort or skill.
example: He never misses a training session, despite having a really demanding job.

en: To promise to give your time or effort to something.
example: Leo was worried about having to commit himself to training sessions every week.

en: Feeling less worried after being comforted.
example: But he felt reassured immediately, as there were other people his age who were only just taking up running for the first time.

en: A person who watches an event.
example: It was only the support of the spectators that kept me going.

en: A feeling of pride after completing something difficult.
example: And it gives you a sense of achievement.

vi: đợt thực tập (làm việc thực tế)
en: A period of working in a company as part of a course.
example: You'll be off to Denmark soon to do your work placement.

en: The part of a book where the pages are joined.
example: He says you have to support the spine, otherwise the paper can come away from the cover.

en: To become worse in condition.
example: I should dump them really, if they're going to deteriorate further, but I'd feel bad.

en: To value something very highly.
example: Maybe it's because I was taught to treasure books.

en: A book with a flexible paper cover.
example: I hate seeing students force open the pages of paperbacks.

en: A book with a stiff cover.
example: Hardbacks aren't quite as weak.

en: Attractive and easy to notice.
example: Some are really eye-catching.

en: The first printing of a book.
example: I guess he treasures things like first editions and other rare books.

en: Set aside for one special purpose.
example: He's got a dedicated area on the ground floor with cushions.

en: A very young child who is learning to walk.
example: So that parents can enter with their toddlers, go there, and spend some time reading to them.

en: To balance something harmful with something good.
example: As well as a way for business corporations to offset their carbon emissions.

en: Planting trees again in an area that has lost its forest.
example: Reforestation projects are currently being undertaken on a huge scale in many countries.

en: At risk of dying out.
example: Including rare and endangered species in order to create a rich ecosystem.

vi: ngoại lai (không có nguồn gốc bản địa)
en: Not originally from a place.
example: It's important to avoid non-native species that could become invasive.

en: Spreading quickly and harming local species.
example: Invasive species are a significant contributor to the current global biodiversity crisis.

en: Easily harmed or damaged.
example: Which can make them vulnerable to disease.

en: The range of different genes within a species.
example: It's vital to use tree seeds with appropriate levels of genetic diversity.

en: Action taken to change a situation.
example: Identifying high-priority areas for intervention is essential.

en: Damaged and reduced in quality.
example: Drone technology is a useful tool in helping to prioritize and monitor areas of degraded forest for restoration.

en: A species that many others in an ecosystem depend on.
example: Figs are a keystone species, because of the critical role they play in maintaining wildlife populations.

en: To spread out over a wide area.
example: Naturally dispersing seeds through defecation.

en: A tropical tree that grows in salty water along coasts.
example: The restoration of mangrove forests in Madagascar is an example of a project which has succeeded in creating real benefits for the community.

en: A person who works to protect nature.
example: According to conservationists, populations of around two thirds of butterfly species have declined in Britain over the past 40 years.

en: The young stage of a butterfly, a long worm-like insect.
example: Butterfly eggs develop into caterpillars.

en: An animal that is hunted and eaten by another.
example: And in turn act as prey for birds as well as bats and other small mammals.

vi: vật hậu học (thời điểm các sự kiện sinh học theo mùa)
en: The study of the timing of natural events such as breeding.
example: Scientists refer to the timing of such lifecycle events as "phenology".

vi: mật độ, số lượng dồi dào
en: A large quantity of something.
example: They then estimated the abundance and distribution of each species across this time.

vi: sự xuất hiện (của bướm trưởng thành)
en: The act of coming out or appearing.
example: Species with more flexible lifecycles were more likely to be able to benefit from an earlier emergence driven by climate change.

vi: được tỉa chồi (rừng cây được cắt tỉa thường xuyên)
en: Cut back regularly so that new shoots grow.
example: It is found only in coppiced woodland and limestone pavement habitats.

en: Able to cause disease.
example: A microbe from a deep-sea sponge was killing pathogenic bugs in his laboratory.

en: An important discovery or achievement.
example: He realised it could be a breakthrough in the fight against antibiotic-resistant superbugs.

en: To think carefully about the good and bad points of something.
example: Asking for time to weigh up the pros and cons.

en: To use something fully for benefit or profit.
example: In sustainability terms, this could be a better way of exploiting the economic potential of the deep sea.

en: Rock from which metal is taken.
example: They say that deep-sea mining could yield far superior ore to land mining with little, if any, waste.

en: Relating to land rather than sea or air.
example: Converted machinery previously used in terrestrial mining.

vi: hệ quả, hậu quả phức tạp
en: A complicated result of an action.
example: Arguing there are potentially massive and unknown ramifications for the environment and for nearby communities.

en: Treating a group as unimportant.
example: And the marginalisation of indigenous peoples and their rights.

en: Originally belonging to a place.
example: And the marginalisation of indigenous peoples and their rights.

vi: miệng phun thủy nhiệt (dưới đáy biển)
en: An opening on the seabed that releases hot water.
example: And hydrothermal vents, which are created when seawater meets volcanic magma.

en: Not yet used.
example: It makes sense to explore this untapped potential in an environmentally sustainable way.

en: To use up so that little remains.
example: Instead of continually looking at the fast depleting land resources of the planet to meet society's rising needs.

en: Hard and cruel, caring only about getting what you want.
example: We're apparently ruthless, with strong impulses to compete against each other for resources and to accumulate power and possessions.

en: A hidden reason for doing something.
example: If we are kind to one another, it's usually because we have ulterior motives.

en: To go beyond a limit.
example: If we are good, it's only because we have managed to control and transcend our innate selfishness and brutality.

vi: tinh thần, hệ giá trị (của một xã hội)
en: The characteristic beliefs of a group or society.
example: Helped to justify the competitive and individualistic ethos that was so prevalent in late 20th-century societies.

en: In small numbers spread over a large area.
example: It's important to remember that in the prehistoric era, the world was very sparsely populated.

en: A person who lives by hunting animals and collecting wild plants.
example: Humans at that time were hunter-gatherers: people who lived by hunting wild animals and collecting wild plants.

en: The belief that all people are equal.
example: Hunter-gatherers are characterised by "extreme political and sexual egalitarianism".

en: To exclude someone from a group.
example: And if a person becomes too domineering, the other members of the group ostracise them.

en: The freedom to make your own decisions.
example: Women in hunter-gatherer groups worldwide often benefit from a high level of autonomy.

en: Caring about others without wanting a reward.
example: It makes more sense, then, to see traits such as cooperation, egalitarianism, altruism and peacefulness as innate characteristics of human beings.

en: Organised in ranks from high to low.
example: They tend to become more violent and hierarchical.

en: Possible and likely to work.
example: It doesn't seem feasible to explain them in adaptive or evolutionary terms.
